note: Single registry of external sources. Problem meta.sources[].name must resolve here (id or alias; interview:<company> is always allowed). Research refs live in refs/<id>.json. verdict: core | supplementary | skip | unreviewed | tag-only (origin tag, not a learning resource).

sources.reason: Problem origin; the canonical judge for most problems.

sources.reason: Problem origin (Blind 75 / NeetCode 150 lists).

sources.name: InterviewBit
sources.reason: Problem origin (2020 legacy solutions).

sources.name: GeeksforGeeks
sources.reason: Problem origin; uneven quality as a learning source.

sources.name: Educative
sources.reason: Origin tag for 2020 solutions; the course is the legacy edition of DesignGurus Grokking.

sources.name: Problem Solving with Algorithms and Data Structures (Runestone)
sources.reason: Problem origin (2018 legacy solutions).

sources.name: DesignGurus — Grokking the Coding Interview
sources.reason: Canonical pattern taxonomy (our catalog's origin), free cheat sheet + a few free intros; mostly paywalled. SD/OOD better covered by ByteByteGo / System Design School.

sources.name: Programiz
sources.reason: Problem origin.

sources.name: w3resource
sources.reason: Problem origin (recursion warm-ups).

sources.name: Wikibooks
sources.reason: Problem origin.

sources.name: Wikipedia
sources.reason: Problem origin / background reading.

sources.name: YouTube
sources.reason: Problem origin (video explanations).

sources.name: Project Euler
sources.reason: Math-heavy practice; not interview-focused.

sources.name: TopCoder / CareerCup
sources.reason: Historic practice source.

sources.name: AlgoMaster
sources.reason: Best visual companion for algo patterns: per-problem step animations with named states and side panels. SD/OOD concepts broad but case studies paywalled; SD practice is code-judged.

sources.name: ByteByteGo
sources.reason: Best system-design learning library: consistent 4-step framework, designs evolved stage by stage, strongest diagrams; ~1/3 of SD chapters readable without login. OOD framework strong. Coding patterns duplicated by its repo.

sources.name: ByteByteGo coding-interview-patterns (GitHub)
sources.reason: Free, well-commented reference solutions (brute force → optimal, DP ladders) per pattern; CC BY-NC-ND so link only. Go is almost absent.

sources.name: Coding Interview University (GitHub)
sources.reason: Mostly dated link lists; its value (fundamentals order, study method, implement-the-API exercises) is folded into resources/ROADMAP.md instead.

sources.name: Tech Interview Handbook
sources.reason: Free study plans, Grind 75 and per-topic corner-case cheatsheets; teaches little itself. SD section is mostly links out.

sources.name: AlgoMonster
sources.reason: Free editorials and cue→technique / input-size→complexity cheatsheets; strong LLD/OOD course. Core pattern families are paid.

sources.name: System Design School
sources.reason: Best free, interactive system-design case studies: numbered skeleton (requirements → estimates → API → data → incremental HLD → deep dives with Bad/Good/Great), live estimators; the model for our SD console.

sources.name: LeetCode Solutions (local PDF)
sources.reason: Copied statements + code-only solutions with no explanations; unclear provenance/licensing. Adds nothing over our READMEs.

sources.name: 20+ Coding Patterns (DesignGurus slide deck, local PDF)
sources.reason: 26-slide DesignGurus promo deck: one slide per Grokking pattern with a usage cue and 2-3 sample names, no teaching. It is our catalog's pattern list and a subset of the free online DesignGurus cheat sheet.

sources.name: Crack The Coding Interview – Must Do Questions 1–500 (Dinesh Varyani, local spreadsheet)
sources.reason: Ranked list of 500 LeetCode links with tags and difficulty; no teaching or solutions. Useful as a backlog for new problems and as an origin tag; no licence stated.
